newsitem.title: USA: CBOT soybeans down on weather, exports support.
newsitem.headline: CBOT soybeans down on weather, exports support.

text.p: Forecasts showing warm, rainy weather continuing in much of the U.S. Midwest weighed on CBOT soybean futures at midsession Monday, traders said.
"The heat we've seen is just what the doctor ordered for the crop," said one commission house trader.
High temperatures climbed into the 80s and 90s (Fahrenheit) over the weekend, and the warmth is needed to speed growth.

More of the same type of weather that prevailed over the weekend was forecast for early this week. Thunderstorms were forecast for Tuesday, and temperatures were seen ranging from 80 to 86 degrees, according to a forecast from Weather Services Corp.
Weekly export shipments for soybeans were greater than expectations, which curbed declines, traders said.
USDA put weekly export inspections of soybeans at 10.022 million bushels. That figure compared with estimates for 3.0 million to 7.0 million bushels.
Cargill and LIT each bought one million bushels July early and Prudential Securities sold one million July, traders said.
At 1121 CDT, July soybeans were down five cents per bushel at $8.21, and other months were down three to 7-1/4 cents.
